newsitem.title: UK: Body Shop H1 profit rise fuelled by Asia.
newsitem.headline: Body Shop H1 profit rise fuelled by Asia.

text.p: Body Shop International Plc, the health and beauty products retailer, reported a 30 percent rise in first half pretax profits on Thursday, fuelled by turnover growth in its key Asian markets.

Pretax profits for the six months to August 31 rose to 11.8 million pounds ($19.14 million) from 9.1 million, with the interim payout growing 39 percent to 1.5 pence. During the period, turnover at the environmentally conscious group rose 11 percent to 117.1 million pounds. Retail sales grew 13 percent to 275.5 million.
Body Shop H1 profit rise fuelled by Asia =2

Chairman Gordon Roddick said there was "strong growth in Asian markets and regeneration in Australia." But he added the U.S. had seen a slowdown leading to a greater loss there and that there were fewer new stores in Europe.

Commenting on current trading conditions, Roddick said like-for-like sales in the first month of the second half were flat on 1995. At the end of the period, Body Shop had 1,436 stores in 46 countries, with Asia described as the "dynamic expansion area."

Looking at a divisional breakdown of the results, UK turnover was 42.9 million pounds versus 41.4 million, with profits stagnant at 2.9 million. In the U.S. turnover was 31.4 million, up from 29.7 million, with the division extending its loss to 3.4 million from 2.4 million last year.

Continental Europe saw turnover at 17.6 million versus 15.0 million, with profits up to 3.1 million from 2.0 million. Asia saw turnover leap to 16.1 million from 11.8 million, with profits up to 6.5 million from 4.5 million.

The rest of the Americas saw turnover of 4.5 million pounds against 4.4 million and profits flat at 1.6 million. Lastly, Australia and new Zealand turnover rose to 4.6 million from 3.1 and profits rose to 1.3 million from 900,000 pounds. ($1=.6165 Pound)
